source_observations.observation: Two differently shaped bases in masculine grammatical examples. A Kāṭhaka citation accompanies the latter.
Saṃ and pari admit kha and retain cha in the Vedic domain.

source_observations.locator: Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 13.15, ed. von Schroeder, p. 198 lines 3–8, TITUS
source_observations.observation: Five datives after undoing regular junctions, followed by a five-member feminine nominative series. The demonstratives iyam and sā fix the agreement.
In the second series this presentation repeats the dative-looking parivatsarāya at the position occupied by the pari adjective in TITUS.
Forms agreeing with svastim, including idā and anu. The petitions name different sacrifices.

source_observations.locator: Bhaṭṭabhāskara on TB 1.4.10, glosses on saṃvatsarīṇām and idāvatsarīṇām
source_observations.observation: The former is explicitly derived through the saṃ/pari prescription. The latter and following instance receive a chāndasa kha qualification.
Nominative plural of the Maruts, with mānuṣeṣu later in the verse.
Same Marut adjective and case, with mānuṣāsaḥ later in this version.
The frog hymn describes the annual brahma that the frogs produce. On Sāyaṇa's syntax the adjective is neuter accusative singular.
Alternative temporal interpretation, at the end of the year.
Four predicates supported by instrumental time. Cloth, illness, vow and building specify the object of each different action.
The commentator accepts both construals of the rule. Supplements distinguish qualifications, practitioners, the rites and a named full moon.
The seasonal sacrifices construct Prajāpati's body. The instrumental and nominative plurals have independently identifiable syntax.
Payment to the officiant. Grammatical support is the genitive of the sacrifice name. Feminine agrees with dakṣiṇā.
Given or done at a time imports the seasonal formation. The split rule also covers food given at a named sacrifice. Kāla scope ends here.
Identifies named locative bases receiving aṇ. The Sanskrit list includes agnipada and pīlumūla where a separate supplement is also discussed.
The rainy-season clouds illustrate the seasonal formation at 4.3.17. The text does not identify a gift or task.
